notes: Curated SF Bay Area benchmark pairs: SF, the East Bay, the Peninsula and Marin. Endpoints are OSM places (2026-10-20 extract), stored snapped to a bicycle edge by check-pairs. Each pair runs in both directions unless one_way is true. Expectations select modes by facets: traffic = quiet|balanced|busy (use_roads 0, 0.5, 1), hills = flat|balanced|tolerant (use_hills 0, 0.75, 1), surface = mixed, plus mode = <scenario>; "*" = every mode. Path and bridge facts were checked against OSM tags and operator or news sources on 2026-10-20. See bench/README.md#pair-catalogs.

pairs.name: Wiggle: Fell to Valencia
pairs.why: The canonical SF flat route through the Wiggle; README example trip.

pairs.name: Castro station to West Portal station (Twin Peaks)
pairs.why: Over the Twin Peaks saddle (Market St / Portola Dr, ~150 m up) or around it; the flat modes should trade distance for climb, the tolerant ones go over.

expect.note: Flat modes go round (1.7-1.9x, saving ~70 m of climb): the trade-off this pair measures.

pairs.name: Glen Park BART to Twin Peaks (Christmas Tree Point)
pairs.why: A climb with no flat alternative (Diamond Heights, Burnett Ave or O'Shaughnessy Blvd): no mode should wander looking for a gentler grade.

pairs.name: Noe Valley (24th & Castro) to Potrero Hill
pairs.why: Release smoke case: across the Mission to the top of Potrero Hill; flat modes should take the valley streets as far as they can.

pairs.name: 16th St Mission BART to 22nd St Caltrain (around Potrero Hill)
pairs.why: Potrero Hill sits between them: flat modes go around it (16th St / Mariposa, or Cesar Chavez), tolerant ones over 20th St.

pairs.name: North Beach to Alamo Square
pairs.why: Release smoke case: Russian Hill and Nob Hill in the way; flat modes should use Columbus / Polk / the valleys rather than climbing.

pairs.name: Civic Center BART to 24th St Mission BART (Valencia)
pairs.why: Valencia St has curbside protected lanes (cycleway:both=track, rebuilt in 2025 when the center-running pilot was removed); quiet modes should take it over Mission St.

expect.note: About 0.3 km at the Market St and 24th St ends, 2026-10-20.

pairs.name: Embarcadero BART to San Francisco City Hall (Market St)
pairs.why: Market St is car-free east of 10th St (motor_vehicle=no, buses and shared lanes) and the direct line; Howard / Folsom protected lanes are the alternative.

expect.note: Quiet modes take Howard/Folsom protected lanes rather than Market's shared bus lanes (1.31x, 2026-10-20).

pairs.name: City Hall to Ghirardelli Square (Polk St)
pairs.why: Polk St bike lanes (part protected) vs Van Ness Ave (busy, BRT); quiet modes should take Polk.

expect.note: Ghirardelli to City Hall: balanced-flat and quiet-flat rode 6.2 km (1.90x) and busy-flat 5.3 km (1.62x) to save ~25 m on Russian Hill, 2026-10-20.

pairs.name: Rincon Park to 16th & Folsom (Folsom St)
pairs.why: Folsom St protected lanes through SoMa vs Harrison / Bryant; the quiet-vs-busy trade-off on a grid of one-way arterials.

pairs.name: Pier 39 to Oracle Park (The Embarcadero)
pairs.why: The Embarcadero (bike lanes, a two-way protected bikeway between Folsom and Mission) is flat and direct; parallel streets climb Telegraph Hill or zig-zag.

pairs.name: Inner Sunset (9th Ave & Irving) to Glen Park BART
pairs.why: Station access across the Twin Peaks / Mt Davidson ridge: 7th Ave / Laguna Honda / Portola vs a long way round.

pairs.name: Daly City BART to SF State (19th Ave)
pairs.why: 19th Ave (CA 1) and I-280 ramps vs Junipero Serra Blvd and residential streets.

pairs.name: Divisadero & Fell to Beach Chalet (Panhandle, JFK Promenade)
pairs.why: The Panhandle path and the JFK Promenade (car-free since 2020, made permanent 2022) run the whole way; quiet modes should stay on them.

pairs.name: Beach Chalet to SF Zoo (Sunset Dunes)
pairs.why: Sunset Dunes, the former Upper Great Highway between Lincoln Way and Sloat Blvd, closed to cars in March 2025 (Prop K) and is a car-free park (OSM highway=pedestrian/cycleway). A November 2026 ballot measure would allow weekday cars again; re-check after it.

expect.note: 0.60 at best: the ends at Fulton St and Sloat Blvd are on streets.

pairs.name: Levi's Plaza to Coit Tower (Filbert Steps)
pairs.why: The direct line is the Filbert Steps; a bike goes round by Lombard St / Telegraph Hill Blvd. Routes should not carry the bike up the stairs.

pairs.name: Palace of Fine Arts to Lyon & Broadway (Lyon Street Steps)
pairs.why: The Lyon Street Steps (Green St to Broadway) are the shortest way up; the rideable streets either side (Baker, Divisadero) are steep too.

pairs.name: Marina Green to the Golden Gate Bridge Welcome Center
pairs.why: Crissy Field promenade and the Presidio; US 101 (Presidio Parkway / Doyle Drive) is a motorway with bikes excluded and must not appear.

expect.note: Busy-flat modes ride 0.5 km of Marina Blvd; US 101 itself is excluded from the graph.

pairs.name: Golden Gate Bridge: Welcome Center to Vista Point (Marin)
pairs.why: Release smoke case: the bridge sidewalks (bicycle=designated; the District rotates bikes between the east and west sidewalks by day and hour, which routing does not model). Every mode must cross directly. Observed 2026-10-20: the six flat and balanced-hill modes take the west sidewalk and loop under the Marin end by the Vista Point Trail (4.8 km, 1.39x); tolerant modes go straight (3.5 km). The DEM has bathymetry under the span (-95 m at mid-span against a ~67 m deck), so routes show ~240 m of false climb; the hill cost likely sees it too.

pairs.name: Ferry Building to Sausalito ferry terminal
pairs.why: The classic tourist ride over the Golden Gate Bridge. use_ferry=0 means the Sausalito ferry must not be taken, and land exists, so no ferry retry.

pairs.name: Pier 39 to Tiburon ferry terminal
pairs.why: Long recreational loop leg (~35 km): Golden Gate Bridge, Sausalito, the Mill Valley-Sausalito path and the Tiburon path. via = Golden Gate Bridge Vista Point.

expect.note: Direct must not be much longer than the route forced over the bridge (the only land link).

pairs.name: Mill Valley Depot to Sausalito ferry terminal (Mill Valley-Sausalito path)
pairs.why: The Mill Valley-Sausalito path along Richardson Bay, the main car-free route in southern Marin, vs US 101 frontage roads.

expect.note: 0.36-0.44: the path covers Richardson Bay; both ends are on streets (Miller Ave, Bridgeway).

pairs.name: Mill Valley Depot to Mt Tamalpais East Peak
pairs.why: Mt Tam approach (about 700 m of climbing): Panoramic Hwy and Pan Toll / Ridgecrest, or Railroad Grade (dirt). Hill-avoiding modes have no flat option. Observed 2026-10-20: busy and quiet flat modes ride 14.8 km (1.47x) with 722 m of climb and 2.9 km of high-stress road, against 10 km and 691 m direct.

expect.note: No flatter route exists.

pairs.name: Larkspur ferry terminal to San Rafael Transit Center (Cal Park tunnel)
pairs.why: The Cal Park Hill Tunnel path (car-free, beside the SMART line) vs Sir Francis Drake Blvd and US 101 interchanges.

pairs.name: Point Reyes Station to Limantour Beach (parking)
pairs.why: Bear Valley Rd and Limantour Rd over Inverness Ridge; the trails across the Phillip Burton Wilderness (bench/areas/sf-wilderness.geojson) are closed to bikes.

expect.note: Every route, the shortest included, has 0.28 km inside the OSM polygon where Limantour Rd ends at the beach parking; more would mean a closed trail.

pairs.name: Tiburon to Angel Island (Ayala Cove)
pairs.why: Release smoke case: no land link, so the land-only request is refused (certified land disconnection) and the adapter's ferry retry takes the Tiburon ferry.

pairs.name: Pier 33 to Alcatraz
pairs.why: Alcatraz has no land link and its ferry (Alcatraz Cruises from Pier 33, this trip's start) is tagged bicycle=no, so no bike route reaches the island. Valhalla moves the island end to the nearest bikeable point, Pier 45 (~1.8 km), and returns a 1.4-2.0 km route along the Embarcadero. That is an acceptable fallback; the rule only keeps it short. The API does not tell the rider the end was moved.

expect.note: The fallback route to Pier 45 is 1.4-2.0 km.

pairs.name: Ferry Building to Treasure Island ferry terminal
pairs.why: The Bay Bridge west span has no bike path, but Treasure Island is joined by land to Yerba Buena Island and the east span path, so with use_ferry=0 the land route goes round by Marin and Richmond (or the Dumbarton Bridge) rather than the 4 km Treasure Island ferry. Observed 2026-10-20: 65-71 km by the northern bridges, 118-126 km by the Dumbarton for busy-flat (both ways) and balanced-flat and quiet-flat (from the island). The 4 km Treasure Island ferry is excluded by use_ferry=0 because land exists.

expect.note: The northern loop is ~65-71 km.

pairs.name: Ferry Building to Jack London Square
pairs.why: The SF-Oakland Bay Bridge west span carries no bikes and the ferry is excluded, so the route is a long land detour (Golden Gate, Richmond-San Rafael bridges or the Dumbarton Bridge). It must not use the bridge. Observed 2026-10-20: tolerant and quiet-balanced modes ride 61-68 km via the Golden Gate and Richmond-San Rafael bridges; flat modes go round by the Dumbarton Bridge instead, 107-113 km (busy-flat both ways, balanced-flat and quiet-flat from Oakland), perhaps to avoid the Golden Gate's false climb.

expect.note: A shorter route would mean the west span (motorway, bicycle=no) was used.
The northern loop is ~61-68 km; the Dumbarton loop is not a sensible choice.

pairs.name: Emeryville to Yerba Buena Island (Bay Bridge Trail)
pairs.why: The Alexander Zuckermann path on the Bay Bridge east span (opening_hours 06:00-21:00 in OSM; routing ignores hours) to the island lookout; the only way there.

pairs.name: Jack London Square to Alameda (Webster St) through the Posey Tube
pairs.why: The Posey Tube's raised sidewalk (bikes allowed both ways by the reviewed access overlay, Oakland-side connectors walk-only) vs the Park St bridge; the Webster St tube is bicycle=no.

pairs.name: Fruitvale BART to Park Street, Alameda
pairs.why: Station access over the Fruitvale or Park St bridge across the Oakland Estuary.

expect.note: Quiet modes cross the Park St bridge and follow the estuary paths to Fruitvale Ave rather than Park St and 29th Ave (1.36x, 2026-10-20).

pairs.name: Rockridge BART to Orinda BART (around the Caldecott Tunnel)
pairs.why: The Caldecott Tunnel (CA 24) is bicycle=no, so the route climbs over the Berkeley hills (Tunnel Rd / Fish Ranch Rd or Claremont Ave). via = Fish Ranch Rd near the summit. Observed 2026-10-20: flat and balanced-hill modes ride 21-36 km (1.7-2.9x) to save 100-200 m; busy-flat Orinda to Rockridge takes 36 km with 28 km of high-stress road.

expect.note: The hills cannot be avoided; a detour over 2x buys little.

pairs.name: Downtown Berkeley BART to the Lawrence Hall of Science
pairs.why: A steep climb through the UC campus and Centennial Dr; no flat alternative exists. Observed 2026-10-20: uphill, the flat and balanced-hill modes ride 8.8-11.6 km (2.1-2.8x) and climb more (334-354 m) than the direct 4.2 km (292 m).

expect.note: No flatter route exists uphill.

pairs.name: Grand Lake to Montclair Village (Oakland hills)
pairs.why: Park Blvd / Mountain Blvd vs the Warren Freeway (CA 13, motorway): hills vs directness with a motorway beside the obvious line. Observed 2026-10-20: quiet-flat takes 3.2 km of high-stress road (7.6 km, 1.59x) to save ~50 m of climb, and downhill both quiet flat and balanced modes ride 1.7 km of it while tolerant ones ride 0.2-0.4 km.

pairs.name: North Berkeley BART to El Cerrito del Norte BART (Ohlone Greenway)
pairs.why: The Ohlone Greenway follows the BART line the whole way; San Pablo Ave is the busy alternative.

pairs.name: Emeryville to the Albany Bulb (Bay Trail)
pairs.why: The Bay Trail beside I-80 through McLaughlin Eastshore State Park vs Frontage Rd and San Pablo Ave.

expect.note: 0.49-0.60: the Emeryville end is on streets.

pairs.name: Walnut Creek BART to Danville (Iron Horse Trail)
pairs.why: The Iron Horse Regional Trail (old Southern Pacific right-of-way) vs Danville Blvd / I-680 frontage roads.

expect.note: About 0.5: the BART station and downtown Danville are each ~1 km off the trail.

pairs.name: Point Richmond to Larkspur Landing (Richmond-San Rafael Bridge)
pairs.why: The bridge's barrier-separated path (open Thursday 2 pm to Sunday night under the pilot extended to 2028; OSM opening_hours agrees, routing ignores it). By land the alternative is round by the Carquinez Strait.

pairs.name: Crockett to Vallejo (Carquinez Bridge Trail)
pairs.why: The Alfred Zampa Memorial Bridge's path is the only bike crossing of the Carquinez Strait here; I-80's other span is bicycle=no.

pairs.name: Martinez Amtrak to Benicia (Benicia-Martinez Bridge path)
pairs.why: The bike and pedestrian path on the 1962 Benicia-Martinez Bridge (southbound I-680) is the only bike crossing at this end of the strait; the 2007 northbound span is bicycle=no.

pairs.name: Belle Haven (Menlo Park) to Newark (Dumbarton Bridge path)
pairs.why: The Dumbarton Bridge's separated path (San Francisco Bay Trail in OSM) is the southernmost bike crossing of the bay.

pairs.name: Foster City to Hayward BART (San Mateo Bridge is closed to bikes)
pairs.why: The San Mateo-Hayward Bridge (CA 92, motorway, bicycle=no) is the direct line; bikes must go round by the Dumbarton Bridge. via = mid-span of the Dumbarton path.

expect.note: A shorter route would mean the San Mateo Bridge was used.

pairs.name: Palo Alto Caltrain to Mountain View Caltrain
pairs.why: Bryant St and Park Blvd bike boulevards vs El Camino Real (busy, part with lanes); quiet modes should keep off El Camino.

pairs.name: Millbrae BART/Caltrain to SFO (around the airport)
pairs.why: Bikes are barred from the main airport roadways but have a marked route from Millbrae Ave along South McDonnell Rd (fly.sfo.gov). Endpoints are where bikesy.com's search puts 'Millbrae BART Parking Garage' and 'San Francisco International Airport (SFO)'. Observed 2026-10-21: 3.4 km via East Millbrae Ave and South McDonnell Rd. A pin dropped on the station building itself snaps to its indoor corridor (way 1492074429), which bikes cannot leave, and gets no route.
